TASK

Using the six supplied reference images, reconstruct this sci-fi hard-surface
column as a clean, editable SketchUp model.

The objective is NOT to create a visually similar interpretation.

The objective is to reconstruct the visible geometry, proportions,
panel divisions, structural layout and mechanical forms of the supplied
references as faithfully and consistently as possible.

The final model will later receive materials manually by me and may
subsequently be exported from SketchUp to Unreal Engine.

DO NOT redesign the object.
DO NOT make it more sci-fi.
DO NOT add creative details that are not supported by the references.


==================================================
REFERENCE IMAGE ROLES
==================================================

Use the six reference images according to these roles:

01_END_A
- Primary reference for one end of the structure.
- Use it to determine footprint, corner geometry, major frame geometry,
  central circular assembly and X-shaped structural organization.

02_PERSPECTIVE_A
- Secondary reference for depth.
- Use it to understand protrusions, recesses, overlaps,
  panel thickness and mechanical connections.

03_PERSPECTIVE_B
- Secondary reference for depth.
- Use together with 02_PERSPECTIVE_A to understand
  the relationship between the vertical body and end assemblies.

04_SIDE_A
- Primary reference for vertical proportions.
- Use for total height-to-width ratio,
  vertical panel divisions,
  top and bottom transitions,
  central rails and major hardware positions.

05_SIDE_B
- Primary reference for the adjacent side.
- Use to verify symmetry,
  vertical alignment,
  panel proportions and differences between adjacent faces.

06_END_B
- Primary reference for the opposite end.
- Use for opposite-end footprint,
  recessed regions,
  central mechanical assembly,
  frame arrangement and corner construction.


==================================================
REFERENCE PRIORITY
==================================================

When different images appear to conflict,
DO NOT randomly average the images.

Use the following hierarchy:

1. END references control end footprint and plan geometry.
2. SIDE references control vertical dimensions and proportions.
3. PERSPECTIVE references control depth, protrusion,
   recesses and part relationships.
4. Large structural geometry has priority over small decorative details.

Never use perspective distortion to determine absolute width or height.

If a small detail differs between images,
preserve the version that is most structurally consistent
with the other references.

If uncertainty remains,
use the simplest reasonable geometry.


==================================================
DIMENSION LIMITATION
==================================================

No absolute real-world measurement has been supplied.

Therefore:

- Preserve the proportions shown in the reference images.
- Do not invent claimed real-world dimensions.
- Work in millimeters.
- Keep the entire object uniformly scalable.
- Maintain consistent relative dimensions throughout the model.

If an absolute height or width is provided later,
the complete model must be capable of being uniformly rescaled
without requiring reconstruction.


==================================================
MODELING OBJECTIVE
==================================================

Create clean SketchUp-native hard-surface geometry.

Do NOT simply create a dense triangulated approximation.

Prefer:

- planar surfaces
- clean extrusions
- controlled offsets
- simple solids
- reusable components
- controlled bevels/chamfers
- clean mechanical construction

The model should remain practical to edit inside SketchUp.


==================================================
MODELING PRIORITY
==================================================

Accuracy must be evaluated in the following exact order:

1. SILHOUETTE
2. PROPORTION
3. STRUCTURAL LAYOUT
4. PANEL LAYOUT
5. DEPTH
6. MAJOR MECHANICAL DETAIL
7. SMALL HARDWARE DETAIL

Never sacrifice silhouette or proportion in order to reproduce
small decorative details.


==================================================
WORKFLOW REQUIREMENT
==================================================

DO NOT attempt to complete the fully detailed model immediately.

The project must be developed in stages.


STAGE 1 — BLOCKOUT

First create ONLY:

- overall bounding volume
- total height-to-width proportions
- main vertical body
- major top/end geometry
- major bottom/opposite-end geometry
- major side panel layout
- main recessed vertical channels

Do NOT add detailed bolts,
small mechanical components,
surface details or decorative hardware yet.


STAGE 2 — BLOCKOUT VALIDATION

Before continuing,
inspect the blockout from views corresponding to ALL SIX references.

Compare:

- silhouette
- total height
- total width
- end footprint
- upper width
- lower width
- main vertical body width
- corner positions
- top transition
- bottom transition
- major panel divisions
- central recessed channels

If any major proportion is incorrect,
correct the blockout BEFORE continuing.

Never compensate for incorrect proportions by adding more detail.


STAGE 3 — PRIMARY STRUCTURE

Only after the blockout is consistent,
add:

- large dark structural frames
- main outer panel geometry
- major recesses
- corner structural elements
- top structural frame
- bottom structural frame
- main central rails
- major mechanical blocks


STAGE 4 — SECONDARY MECHANICAL DETAIL

Then add:

- central circular mechanisms
- rail components
- large connectors
- major brackets
- visible mechanical inserts
- significant bolts and fasteners


STAGE 5 — BEVEL AND CLEANUP

Only after geometry is correct,
apply appropriate bevels/chamfers,
clean geometry,
check intersections,
check reversed faces,
and organize groups/components.


==================================================
SYMMETRY
==================================================

The structure appears to contain significant
four-way rotational repetition.

Where the reference images confirm identical geometry:

1. Accurately model one repeated module.
2. Convert it into a SketchUp Component.
3. Rotate-copy it around the vertical center axis,
   typically in 90-degree increments.

Do NOT manually remodel identical repeated components.

This is important for maintaining consistent dimensions.

However:

Do NOT force four-way symmetry where the references clearly show
different geometry.

Differences shown in the reference images must be preserved.


==================================================
MAIN BODY
==================================================

Accurately reproduce:

- tall vertical column proportion
- main exterior panels
- central dark vertical channels
- corner transitions
- widened upper structure
- widened lower structure
- visible structural segmentation

Do not simplify the main silhouette into a basic rectangular column.

The characteristic widening,
corner cuts and panel transitions
must remain recognizable.


==================================================
END GEOMETRY
==================================================

Use 01_END_A and 06_END_B as the primary references
for the two ends.

Preserve:

- overall footprint
- chamfered corners
- large dark perimeter frames
- X-shaped structural composition where visible
- central circular assembly
- recessed areas
- major mechanical connectors
- corner blocks

Do not assume END_A and END_B are identical
unless the references confirm that they are identical.


==================================================
SIDE GEOMETRY
==================================================

Use 04_SIDE_A and 05_SIDE_B as the primary elevation references.

Preserve:

- vertical panel proportions
- black vertical central channels
- major panel seams
- widened top transition
- widened bottom transition
- vertical mechanical rails
- major fastener positions
- dark structural strips

Keep vertical alignment consistent from top to bottom.


==================================================
PANEL CONSTRUCTION
==================================================

Large exterior panels must remain identifiable
as separate construction zones.

Do not model the entire side surface as one undifferentiated face.

Preserve:

- panel boundaries
- major panel seams
- recessed central channels
- top panel transitions
- bottom panel transitions
- corner panel transitions

Major panel geometry that may later receive
a different material should remain independently selectable.


==================================================
RECESSES
==================================================

Pay particular attention to dark recessed regions.

A dark area in the reference image does NOT automatically mean
an empty through-hole.

Unless the reference clearly shows a true opening,
construct the recess as:

front opening
→ side walls
→ rear/back surface

Do NOT leave undefined infinitely deep cavities.


==================================================
OPENINGS AND BACK PLATES
==================================================

No accidental open holes are allowed.

Any visible recess that exposes undefined empty space
must be closed with appropriate geometry.

If detailed internal machinery is not visible or not necessary,
use a simple back plate.

Do NOT create complex invisible machinery merely to fill a cavity.

The exterior visual result is the priority.


==================================================
CLOSED GEOMETRY
==================================================

Where practical,
major structural parts should behave as closed solids.

Do not leave missing rear surfaces
simply because they are not visible in one image.

Remove unintended:

- open edges
- missing faces
- incomplete panels
- broken shells


==================================================
DO NOT INVENT HIDDEN DETAIL
==================================================

Hidden geometry is ambiguous because only six reference images are supplied.

When hidden information is unavailable:

use the simplest geometry that correctly connects
the visible surfaces.

DO NOT invent:

- pipes
- cables
- vents
- random armor
- additional sci-fi panels
- additional bolts
- extra openings
- extra lights
- decorative machinery
- fictional internal mechanisms

unless they are clearly supported by the supplied references.


==================================================
DEPTH ESTIMATION
==================================================

Use BOTH perspective images to estimate depth.

Use them to judge:

- panel thickness
- frame thickness
- rail projection
- recess depth
- end-cap depth
- overlap between parts
- protruding mechanical components

Do not exaggerate depth due to perspective distortion.

Depth relationships should remain consistent
around all sides of the model.


==================================================
BEVELS AND CHAMFERS
==================================================

The reference object uses hard-surface chamfered geometry.

Do not leave all exterior edges as infinitely sharp 90-degree edges.

Apply controlled bevels/chamfers to major visible edges,
especially:

- outer frame edges
- corner structures
- top structural frame
- bottom structural frame
- main panel borders
- large mechanical blocks
- central mechanical components
- major vertical rails

Use low-to-moderate bevel segmentation.

Do NOT create unnecessarily dense rounded geometry.


==================================================
CURVED AND CIRCULAR PARTS
==================================================

Circular mechanical details should remain visually circular
but should not use excessive polygon counts.

Use an appropriate SketchUp segment count.

The central circular mechanisms,
large fasteners and similar hardware
must remain clean and centered.

Do NOT use extremely high-poly cylinders.


==================================================
FASTENERS
==================================================

Bolts, screws and circular fasteners are secondary details.

Use reusable SketchUp Components.

Create only the number of unique fastener types that are necessary.

Duplicate components where appropriate.

Do NOT individually model every identical bolt from scratch.

Do NOT model:

- screw threads
- microscopic grooves
- invisible internal bolt geometry


==================================================
MICRO DETAIL
==================================================

Do NOT model surface details that do not meaningfully affect silhouette,
depth or visible shadows.

Do NOT model:

- surface grain
- scratches
- paint wear
- tiny engraved text
- printed warning graphics
- tiny logos
- microscopic panel grooves
- microscopic screw detail

These will later be handled using materials and textures.


==================================================
MATERIALS
==================================================

I WILL APPLY ALL FINAL MATERIALS MYSELF.

Do NOT spend time creating final materials.

Do NOT create:

- PBR materials
- texture maps
- Base Color maps
- Normal maps
- Roughness maps
- Metallic maps
- AO maps
- Emissive materials
- complex UV textures

Use SketchUp Default Material for the model.

Do not randomly color individual surfaces.


==================================================
GEOMETRY MUST STILL BE MATERIAL-READY
==================================================

Although final materials are not required,
surfaces that are likely to receive different materials later
must remain independently selectable.

Do NOT permanently merge geometrically distinct surface zones.

For example,
keep the following separately selectable when applicable:

- main exterior panels
- dark structural frames
- mechanical rails
- central mechanisms
- trim pieces
- inset components
- hardware
- rear/back plates

I must be able to assign different materials later
without rebuilding the model.


==================================================
RECOMMENDED SKETCHUP HIERARCHY
==================================================

Organize the model approximately as:

SCI_FI_COLUMN_MASTER

    01_MAIN_BODY
        Main_Panels
        Upper_Transition
        Lower_Transition

    02_DARK_STRUCTURAL_FRAME
        Upper_Frame
        Lower_Frame
        Corner_Frames
        Side_Frames

    03_VERTICAL_MECHANICAL
        Vertical_Rails
        Center_Channel
        Mechanical_Inserts

    04_END_A_ASSEMBLY
        EndA_Frame
        EndA_Center
        EndA_Mechanical

    05_END_B_ASSEMBLY
        EndB_Frame
        EndB_Center
        EndB_Mechanical

    06_HARDWARE
        Bolts
        Circular_Fasteners
        Connectors

    07_BACK_PLATES
        Recess_Back_Plates


This hierarchy may be adjusted if necessary,
but equivalent functional separation must be preserved.


==================================================
GROUPING RULES
==================================================

All meaningful geometry must belong to
a SketchUp Group or Component.

Do not leave loose raw geometry at the root level.

Use Groups for unique assemblies.

Use Components for repeated objects.

Recommended Component candidates include:

- repeated corner structures
- repeated rails
- repeated brackets
- repeated fasteners
- rotationally repeated structural elements

Do not create hundreds of unnecessary groups
for individual faces or tiny details.

Grouping should follow:

- construction logic
- repeated geometry
- future material zones
- editing convenience


==================================================
FACE ORIENTATION
==================================================

All visible exterior faces must face outward.

Inspect the entire model for reversed faces.

Correct all reversed exterior surfaces.

Do not depend on two-sided material rendering
to hide incorrect face orientation.

This is required for later Unreal Engine export.


==================================================
DUPLICATE AND COPLANAR GEOMETRY
==================================================

There must be NO duplicate faces
occupying the same position.

There must be NO unnecessary coplanar overlapping surfaces.

Avoid Z-fighting.

Remove:

- duplicate faces
- duplicate edges
- accidental overlapping panels
- hidden duplicates
- floating edges
- isolated geometry
- unused internal copies


==================================================
INTERSECTIONS
==================================================

Check all major assemblies for unintended intersections.

Pay particular attention to:

- upper frame connections
- lower frame connections
- corner structures
- central vertical rails
- side panel transitions
- central circular mechanisms
- fasteners
- structural brackets

Parts may intentionally connect,
but unrelated solids must not randomly pass through one another.


==================================================
INTERNAL GEOMETRY
==================================================

Do not create unnecessary hidden internal geometry.

Internal geometry is required only when necessary to:

- close visible recesses
- support an opening
- prevent visible holes
- maintain a clean solid
- support a visible mechanical component

Otherwise,
keep the model lightweight.


==================================================
TOPOLOGY
==================================================

Do NOT prioritize reproducing arbitrary topology.

Prioritize:

- correct visible geometry
- clean SketchUp construction
- simple editable forms
- consistent dimensions
- reliable grouping

Avoid unnecessarily complicated triangulated surfaces
when a simple planar face can reproduce the same shape.

Do not create dense geometry merely to imitate rendered shading.


==================================================
SMOOTHING
==================================================

Use SketchUp smoothing/softening appropriately
for genuinely curved or faceted transitions.

Do NOT soften structural panel boundaries
that should remain visibly sharp.

Maintain hard edges at intentional panel divisions.


==================================================
MODEL PERFORMANCE
==================================================

The model must remain practical to use in SketchUp.

Avoid unnecessary polygon density.

Use Components for repeated details.

Do not model invisible detail.

Preserve the visual form without creating
unnecessarily heavy geometry.


==================================================
AXIS AND ORIGIN
==================================================

Use Z as the vertical axis.

Center the object around the SketchUp world origin.

Place the lowest physical point at:

Z = 0

Keep the main vertical center axis aligned
with the SketchUp vertical axis.

Maintain clean and predictable orientation
for later export to Unreal Engine.


==================================================
BACKGROUND
==================================================

The white backgrounds,
render lighting,
shadows and empty surrounding space
shown in the six reference images
are NOT part of the object.

Do NOT model them.


==================================================
FINAL VISUAL VALIDATION
==================================================

Before finalizing,
compare the SketchUp model against ALL SIX reference images.

Inspect corresponding views for:

- END_A
- END_B
- SIDE_A
- SIDE_B
- PERSPECTIVE_A
- PERSPECTIVE_B

First compare silhouette.

Then verify:

1. overall height-to-width ratio
2. end footprint
3. corner positions
4. top width and geometry
5. bottom width and geometry
6. upper transition
7. lower transition
8. major panel positions
9. central recessed channel positions
10. vertical rail positions
11. large structural frame thickness
12. rotational alignment
13. central circular assembly positions
14. major bolt locations
15. recess depth
16. panel thickness
17. bevel consistency


==================================================
FINAL GEOMETRY VALIDATION
==================================================

Before saving,
inspect the full SketchUp model and verify:

1. No unintended open holes.
2. No missing back surfaces behind recesses.
3. No reversed exterior faces.
4. No loose geometry at the root level.
5. No duplicate faces.
6. No coplanar overlapping faces.
7. No random object intersections.
8. No unnecessary hidden internal geometry.
9. Repeated geometry uses Components where appropriate.
10. Repeated components have consistent dimensions.
11. Major four-way repeated structures align correctly.
12. Main panels remain independently selectable.
13. Structural frames remain independently selectable.
14. Mechanical components remain independently selectable.
15. Back plates remain independently selectable where required.
16. Model is centered correctly.
17. Lowest point is at Z = 0.
18. Vertical center axis is aligned with Z.
19. Model remains easily editable in SketchUp.
20. Materials can later be assigned without remodeling.
21. Model remains suitable for later export to Unreal Engine.


==================================================
FINAL RULE
==================================================

DO NOT reinterpret the design.

DO NOT redesign the model.

DO NOT add creative sci-fi detail.

DO NOT prioritize small details over structural accuracy.

If any reference information is ambiguous,
compare all six images before making a decision.

If the ambiguity cannot be resolved,
use the simplest geometrically reasonable solution
that is consistent with the visible references.

Always preserve the following priority:

SILHOUETTE
→ PROPORTION
→ STRUCTURAL LAYOUT
→ PANEL LAYOUT
→ DEPTH
→ MAJOR MECHANICAL DETAIL
→ SECONDARY DETAIL


==================================================
FINAL COMPLETION PROCEDURE
==================================================

Before considering the task complete:

A. Return to the simplified blockout logic mentally
   and verify that the final detailed model still matches
   the original large-scale proportions.

B. Temporarily ignore small details and compare
   only the silhouette against all six references.

C. If the silhouette or major proportions are incorrect,
   correct the geometry even if detailed components
   must be repositioned.

D. Confirm that added detail has not distorted
   the original blockout.

E. Only after silhouette, proportion and structure are correct
   should the model be considered complete.

Accuracy of the primary geometry is more important
than the quantity of detail.

TASK

Using the four supplied reference images, reconstruct this rectangular sci-fi
hard-surface panel as a clean, editable SketchUp model.

The objective is NOT to create a similar-looking interpretation.

The objective is to reproduce the visible geometry, proportions,
panel segmentation, thickness, grooves, recessed channels and
major mechanical details as faithfully as possible.

The final model will later receive materials manually by me
and may subsequently be exported from SketchUp to Unreal Engine.

DO NOT redesign the object.
DO NOT add new sci-fi details.
DO NOT invent decorative geometry.


==================================================
REFERENCE IMAGE ROLES
==================================================

Use the four supplied images according to the following roles.


IMAGE 01 — TOP / PRIMARY PLAN REFERENCE

Use this image as the PRIMARY reference for:

- overall length-to-width ratio
- outer rectangular silhouette
- left/right symmetry
- central dark strip width
- side panel widths
- vent strip locations
- panel divisions
- blue light locations
- corner details
- chamfered panel boundaries

This image controls the plan geometry.


IMAGE 02 — PERSPECTIVE REFERENCE

Use this image primarily to understand:

- thickness
- raised vs recessed surfaces
- panel layering
- side-edge construction
- vent depth
- central strip depth
- blue light recess depth
- panel bevels
- relative height differences between surfaces

Do NOT use perspective distortion to determine overall width or length.


IMAGE 03 — SHORT-END SIDE REFERENCE

Use this image to determine:

- total panel thickness
- front-edge profile
- height of raised and recessed layers
- short-side segmentation
- blue light housing geometry
- edge chamfers

This image controls the short-end side profile.


IMAGE 04 — LONG-SIDE REFERENCE

Use this image to determine:

- total thickness
- long-side edge profile
- long-side panel segmentation
- central light housing
- end blocks
- long-side chamfers

This image controls the long-side edge profile.


==================================================
REFERENCE PRIORITY
==================================================

If references appear inconsistent:

1. IMAGE 01 controls plan dimensions and layout.
2. IMAGE 03 and IMAGE 04 control thickness and side profiles.
3. IMAGE 02 controls depth, layering and recess interpretation.
4. Small decorative inconsistencies have lower priority than the main form.

Never average conflicting geometry randomly.

Use the simplest geometry that is consistent with the majority
of the reference information.


==================================================
WORKFLOW REQUIREMENT
==================================================

DO NOT build all details immediately.

Work in the following stages.


STAGE 1 — BLOCKOUT

First create only:

- overall rectangular base
- total length-to-width proportion
- total thickness
- central longitudinal strip
- left and right main panel zones
- edge profile
- basic major panel divisions

Do NOT add vents, lights or small grooves yet.


STAGE 2 — BLOCKOUT VALIDATION

Compare the blockout against all four references.

Verify:

- overall silhouette
- length-to-width ratio
- total thickness
- central strip width
- left/right panel widths
- short-end profile
- long-side profile

Correct any major proportion errors BEFORE continuing.


STAGE 3 — PRIMARY PANEL GEOMETRY

Add:

- major white side panels
- dark central panels
- side dark inset strips
- primary seams
- major chamfers
- central recessed zones


STAGE 4 — SECONDARY DETAIL

Then add:

- vent channels
- blue light housings
- small recessed slots
- small circular holes
- panel cuts
- minor frame details


STAGE 5 — CLEANUP

After geometry is correct:

- apply controlled bevels
- close unintended openings
- remove duplicates
- check face orientation
- organize groups/components
- verify editability


==================================================
MAIN FORM
==================================================

The object is a thin rectangular hard-surface panel.

Preserve:

- long rectangular proportion
- low overall thickness
- symmetrical left and right major panel layout
- dark central longitudinal strip
- paired vent strips
- angular side-panel cut lines
- recessed light housings
- thin layered construction

Do NOT exaggerate thickness.

Do NOT make the object look like a thick platform or box.


==================================================
SYMMETRY
==================================================

The top view shows strong bilateral symmetry.

Where geometry is clearly mirrored:

- model one side accurately
- use mirrored Groups or Components where appropriate

However:

do NOT force the short-end side profile
and long-side profile to be identical.

They are different edges of the same rectangular object.


==================================================
CENTRAL STRIP
==================================================

The central dark longitudinal strip is a major structural feature.

Preserve:

- its width
- its continuous longitudinal alignment
- panel segmentation
- recessed light modules
- slight depth separation from adjacent panels

Do not merge the central strip into the side panels.


==================================================
VENT STRIPS
==================================================

There are narrow repeated vent/slat strips
running along both sides of the central strip.

Treat these as separate geometry zones.

The visible vent repetition should be modeled efficiently.

Prefer:

- one repeated slat Component
or
- a simplified repeated array

Do NOT individually create hundreds of unrelated unique slats.

Keep the vent depth shallow and consistent with the perspective reference.


==================================================
SIDE PANELS
==================================================

The large light-colored side surfaces must be modeled as
separate panel regions.

Preserve:

- major angular cuts
- large rectangular divisions
- darker outer inset panels
- light housings
- panel seams
- small visible openings

Do not model the entire side surface as one large undivided slab.


==================================================
LIGHT MODULES
==================================================

The blue illuminated regions must remain
independently selectable geometry.

I will apply the emissive material myself.

Create only the physical geometry:

- light recess
- surrounding frame/housing
- flat light-emitting surface

Do NOT create actual blue materials or emissive shaders.

Keep the light-emitting surface separated from its housing.


==================================================
MATERIALS
==================================================

I WILL APPLY ALL MATERIALS MYSELF.

Do NOT create final materials.

Do NOT create:

- PBR materials
- Base Color maps
- Normal maps
- Roughness maps
- Metallic maps
- AO maps
- emissive shaders
- UV texture assets

Use SketchUp Default Material.

Do not paint groups or individual faces with arbitrary colors.


==================================================
MATERIAL-READY GEOMETRY
==================================================

Even though materials are not required,
geometry that may receive different materials later
must remain separately selectable.

Keep at least these zones separated:

01_MAIN_LIGHT_PANELS
02_DARK_CENTER_PANELS
03_DARK_SIDE_INSETS
04_VENT_GEOMETRY
05_LIGHT_SURFACES
06_LIGHT_HOUSINGS
07_SMALL_HARDWARE
08_BASE_STRUCTURE

Do not permanently merge all parts into one mesh.


==================================================
RECOMMENDED SKETCHUP HIERARCHY
==================================================

SCI_FI_PANEL_MASTER

    01_BASE
        Main_Base

    02_SIDE_PANELS
        Left_Panels
        Right_Panels

    03_CENTER_STRIP
        Center_Main
        Center_Sections

    04_VENTS
        Left_Vents
        Right_Vents

    05_SIDE_INSETS
        Left_Insets
        Right_Insets

    06_LIGHTS
        Light_Surfaces
        Light_Housings

    07_SMALL_DETAILS
        Slots
        Holes
        Minor_Hardware


Use Groups for unique geometry.

Use Components for repeated identical objects.


==================================================
CLOSED GEOMETRY
==================================================

All visible structural parts should be closed
where practical.

Do NOT leave accidental holes.

Recessed areas should contain:

opening
→ side walls
→ rear surface

unless the reference clearly shows a through-hole.

Do not leave infinitely deep cavities.


==================================================
DEPTH
==================================================

Use IMAGE 02, IMAGE 03 and IMAGE 04
to estimate depth relationships.

Important depth levels include:

- main base
- raised side panels
- recessed center strip
- vent recess
- dark outer inset panels
- light housings
- light surfaces

Keep these depth differences subtle.

This is a thin hard-surface panel,
not a deeply layered mechanical structure.


==================================================
BEVELS
==================================================

Apply small controlled bevels/chamfers
to visible hard-surface edges.

Use bevels on:

- outer perimeter
- large side panels
- central panel edges
- light housings
- large inset panels
- raised strips

Keep bevels subtle.

Do NOT excessively round edges.

Avoid perfectly sharp unrealistic 90-degree edges
where the reference clearly shows chamfers.


==================================================
MICRO DETAIL
==================================================

Do NOT model unnecessary micro detail.

Do not model:

- surface scratches
- paint texture
- tiny wear marks
- microscopic grooves
- fine material grain
- invisible underside hardware

Only model details that create
a clearly visible change in silhouette,
depth or shadow.


==================================================
SMALL HOLES / SLOTS
==================================================

Small circular dots and narrow slots visible on the surface
may be represented as shallow recesses.

Do not create unnecessary complex internal geometry.

Do not model deep holes unless clearly visible.


==================================================
FACE ORIENTATION
==================================================

All exterior faces must face outward.

Inspect the entire model for reversed faces.

Correct all reversed exterior faces.

Do not rely on double-sided rendering.


==================================================
DUPLICATE GEOMETRY
==================================================

Remove:

- duplicate faces
- duplicate edges
- overlapping coplanar faces
- floating geometry
- isolated edges
- hidden unnecessary duplicates

No Z-fighting is allowed.


==================================================
INTERSECTIONS
==================================================

Check:

- central strip
- side panels
- vent strips
- light housings
- outer inset panels
- edge blocks

No unrelated geometry may randomly pass through another part.


==================================================
MODEL PERFORMANCE
==================================================

Keep the SketchUp model lightweight.

Avoid excessive polygon count.

Use Components for repeated vent slats
and repeated small details.

Do not over-model invisible geometry.


==================================================
AXIS AND ORIGIN
==================================================

Place the object centered near the SketchUp world origin.

Use:

- X axis = long direction
- Y axis = short direction
- Z axis = thickness / vertical direction

Place the lowest point of the object at:

Z = 0

Keep the model flat and level.


==================================================
BACKGROUND
==================================================

The dark background,
lighting and shadows visible in the reference images
are NOT part of the model.

Do NOT model them.


==================================================
FINAL VISUAL VALIDATION
==================================================

Before completion,
compare the SketchUp model against all four references.

Check in this order:

1. top silhouette
2. overall length-to-width ratio
3. total thickness
4. central strip width
5. side-panel width
6. outer edge geometry
7. vent positions

- repeated Components

[ASTRA 6 MEDIUM — HIGH PRECISION SPIRAL HANDRAIL MODELING]

TASK:
Create ONLY the handrail / guardrail system shown in the attached Rhino reference images.

The reference images show the same helical / spiral stair geometry from multiple viewpoints.

Use all provided views together to reconstruct the railing path accurately.

IMPORTANT:
The stair itself is reference geometry only.

DO NOT remodel the staircase.
DO NOT remodel the stair treads.
DO NOT remodel the central stair structure.

Create ONLY:

1. vertical railing posts / balusters
2. continuous upper handrail
3. necessary connection geometry between the posts and handrail

The final output must be suitable for SketchUp (.SKP).

============================================================
1. PRIMARY REFERENCE LOGIC
============================================================

The railing must follow the exact outer path of the spiral staircase visible in the Rhino reference images.

Do NOT replace the existing geometry with a generic circular spiral.

Do NOT create a mathematically perfect helix unless it matches the reference.

Use the reference geometry to determine:

- railing horizontal path
- spiral curvature
- vertical progression
- start point
- end point
- local changes in direction
- relationship between each stair tread and railing post
- continuous handrail trajectory

The reference stair geometry defines the railing path.

The railing should visually align with the outer perimeter of the stair.

============================================================
2. FIXED DIMENSIONS — DO NOT MODIFY
============================================================

The following dimensions are fixed and must be followed exactly.

RAILING HEIGHT:
15 mm

HANDRAIL THICKNESS:
1.5 mm

Do NOT scale these dimensions automatically.

Do NOT reinterpret them based on architectural standards.

Use the values exactly as specified.

============================================================
3. RAILING HEIGHT
============================================================

Every vertical railing post must rise:

15 mm

vertically from its corresponding mounting position.

Measure the height vertically in world Z direction.

Do NOT measure 15 mm along the slope of the staircase.

Correct:

base point
→ vertical Z direction
→ 15 mm

All primary railing posts should have consistent height unless the reference clearly requires a different termination condition.

============================================================
4. HANDRAIL
============================================================

Create a continuous upper handrail following the top points of the vertical railing posts.

HANDRAIL THICKNESS:
1.5 mm

Prefer a clean circular section unless the reference geometry clearly indicates another profile.

Recommended:

circular handrail
diameter = 1.5 mm

The handrail must:

- remain continuous
- follow the helical stair path
- maintain smooth curvature
- pass through or connect consistently to the top of the posts
- maintain the same section size throughout
- rise continuously with the staircase

Do NOT create the handrail as disconnected short segments.

The visual result must read as ONE continuous flowing rail.

============================================================
5. HANDRAIL PATH
============================================================

The handrail path is extremely important.

Follow the outer edge of the stair path shown in the reference.

The handrail must reproduce:

- circular / spiral progression in plan
- vertical progression in elevation
- multiple turns around the central axis
- transitions between each stair level
- top and bottom termination points

Do not flatten the handrail.

Do not make the rail horizontal.

Do not create separate circular rings for each level.

It must be one continuous three-dimensional spiral curve.

============================================================
6. VERTICAL POSTS / BALUSTERS
============================================================

Create vertical posts along the outer stair edge as shown in the reference.

Each post must:

- remain vertical in world Z
- begin at the outer stair / railing base position
- extend upward exactly 15 mm
- connect to the continuous upper handrail

Do NOT tilt the posts to follow the stair slope.

Posts remain vertical.

The stair and rail rise around them.

============================================================
7. POST POSITIONING
============================================================

Use the Rhino reference images to determine post positions.

Posts appear repeatedly along the outer edge of the stair.

Prioritize alignment with the stair modules / tread locations visible in the reference.

Do NOT distribute the posts randomly.

Do NOT create arbitrary equal spacing if it conflicts with the reference.

Where possible:

one repeated post position should correspond consistently to the stair module pattern.

Maintain the visual rhythm shown in the original Rhino model.

============================================================
8. POST PROFILE
============================================================

Keep the posts simple.

Do not create decorative railing posts.

Use a minimal straight structural profile.

Unless another profile is clearly visible in the reference, use a simple narrow circular or rectangular section.

The railing must remain visually lightweight.

Do NOT make the posts excessively thick.

Do NOT introduce ornamental details.

============================================================
9. PLAN VIEW ACCURACY
============================================================

The supplied top view is critical.

Use it to preserve the circular / helical plan geometry.

The railing path must maintain the correct relationship between:

- inner stair opening
- stair outer perimeter
- outer railing path

The railing must remain on the OUTER side of the spiral stair.

Do not move the railing toward the center opening.

Do not change the spiral radius arbitrarily.

============================================================
10. ELEVATION ACCURACY
============================================================

Use the side and perspective views to reconstruct the vertical progression.

The railing must rise continuously with the staircase.

Preserve the number of visible spiral rotations and the approximate pitch shown in the references.

Do NOT compress the vertical spacing.

Do NOT stretch the spiral vertically.

Do NOT change the number of turns.

Use the Rhino images as the primary geometric reference.

============================================================
11. START / END CONDITIONS
============================================================

Follow the visible start and end points from the reference.

At the lowest stair:

terminate the railing cleanly at the beginning of the stair flight.

At the highest stair:

terminate the handrail cleanly at the end of the visible stair flight.

Do not extend the rail beyond the reference.

Do not add decorative end caps unless necessary for closed geometry.

============================================================
12. GEOMETRY REQUIREMENTS
============================================================

All railing parts must be actual 3D geometry.

Do NOT use:

- lines only
- curves only
- construction guides
- 2D profiles without thickness

The final SKP model must contain physical solid geometry.

Handrail:
closed tubular or solid profile

Posts:
closed solid geometry

No open faces.

No broken surfaces.

============================================================
13. CURVE QUALITY
============================================================

The continuous upper handrail must appear smooth.

Use enough segments to preserve the spiral curve when imported into SketchUp.

However:

Do NOT create excessive segmentation.

Avoid unnecessarily dense geometry.

Use an efficient curve resolution that maintains a visually smooth handrail.

Avoid faceted or visibly polygonal curvature.

============================================================
14. OBJECT SEPARATION
============================================================

Do NOT merge the entire railing into one raw mesh.

Each primary physical component must remain independently editable.

Recommended individual objects:

OBJ_HANDRAIL_MAIN

OBJ_POST_001
OBJ_POST_002
OBJ_POST_003
OBJ_POST_004
OBJ_POST_005
...

If multiple disconnected handrail sections are truly necessary:

OBJ_HANDRAIL_SECTION_01
OBJ_HANDRAIL_SECTION_02

However, prefer one continuous handrail whenever possible.

============================================================
15. REQUIRED GROUP HIERARCHY
============================================================

Use a clean SketchUp-compatible hierarchy.

Required logic:

INDIVIDUAL GEOMETRY
→ INDIVIDUAL OBJECT / GROUP
→ COMPONENT GROUP
→ MAT_NONE
→ MASTER GROUP

Required hierarchy:

MASTER_SPIRAL_HANDRAIL
│
└── MAT_NONE
    │
    ├── GRP_HANDRAIL
    │   └── OBJ_HANDRAIL_MAIN
    │
    └── GRP_VERTICAL_POSTS
        ├── OBJ_POST_001
        ├── OBJ_POST_002
        ├── OBJ_POST_003
        ├── OBJ_POST_004
        ├── OBJ_POST_005
        └── ...

Every vertical post must remain individually selectable.

Do not explode all posts into raw geometry.

============================================================
16. MATERIAL RULES
============================================================

NO MATERIALS.

This task is geometry only.

Do not assign:

- metal
- steel
- black material
- white material
- glass
- paint
- texture
- color
- roughness
- metallic shader
- emissive material

All geometry must use:

Material = NONE / Default / Unassigned

MAT_NONE is only a hierarchy / organizational group.

MAT_NONE is NOT an actual material.

============================================================
17. SKETCHUP REQUIREMENTS
============================================================

The final model will be used directly in SketchUp.

Therefore:

- keep every post as a separate group/component
- keep the main handrail as a separate group
- prevent raw geometry from sticking to adjacent geometry
- avoid unnecessary nested groups
- use clear object names
- maintain editable geometry
- preserve real-world dimensions
- keep axes consistent
- ensure correct face orientation

All front faces should point outward.

No reversed faces should remain visible.

============================================================
18. MODEL CLEANUP
============================================================

Before export, verify:

- no duplicate posts
- no overlapping handrail geometry
- no disconnected handrail segments
- no floating vertices
- no loose edges
- no duplicate faces
- no internal accidental faces
- no non-manifold geometry
- no broken circular profiles
- no unnecessary triangulation
- no accidental merged stair geometry

============================================================
19. DO NOT MODEL THE STAIRS
============================================================

This is extremely important.

The stair visible in the reference images is ONLY used to determine the railing path.

DO NOT include:

- stair treads
- risers
- staircase frame
- central column
- floor slabs
- staircase support structure

Final output:

HANDRAIL / GUARDRAIL ONLY.

============================================================
20. DO NOT ADD NEW DESIGN ELEMENTS
============================================================

Do not add:

- horizontal middle rails
- glass panels
- wire cables
- mesh panels
- decorative rail elements
- brackets not shown
- extra balusters
- ornamental elements

Reproduce only the railing system visible in the Rhino reference.

============================================================
21. PRIORITY ORDER
============================================================

If any reference information is ambiguous, use this priority:

1. fixed dimensions supplied in the prompt
2. top-view railing trajectory
3. vertical progression visible in side views
4. post positions visible in multiple views
5. perspective appearance

Never override:

15 mm railing height
1.5 mm handrail thickness

============================================================
22. FINAL ACCEPTANCE CHECK
============================================================

Before finalizing, verify:

[ ] Only railing geometry was modeled

[ ] Stair geometry was NOT included

[ ] Railing follows the outer perimeter of the reference staircase

[ ] Spiral trajectory matches the supplied Rhino views

[ ] Number of spiral turns matches the reference

[ ] Vertical progression matches the reference

[ ] All posts are vertical

[ ] Every post height = exactly 15 mm

[ ] Handrail thickness = exactly 1.5 mm

[ ] Upper handrail is continuous

[ ] Handrail follows the top of the vertical posts

[ ] No random post placement

[ ] Individual posts are separately selectable

[ ] Handrail is separately selectable

[ ] Geometry is grouped correctly

[ ] All objects are inside component groups

[ ] All component groups are inside MAT_NONE

[ ] MAT_NONE is inside MASTER_SPIRAL_HANDRAIL

[ ] No material is assigned

[ ] No texture is assigned

[ ] No extra design elements are added

[ ] Geometry is clean and SketchUp-ready

FINAL OUTPUT:

ONE clean spiral handrail / guardrail assembly based on the supplied Rhino reference.

SKP

MODEL:
HANDRAIL ONLY

HANDRAIL THICKNESS = 1.5 mm

NONE

CLEAN, EDITABLE, GROUPED
